messages:
Erin: Quick heads-up — ran a full perf sweep this morning for mixtral-8x with paged KV enabled + GQA/MQA switches. Seeing a consistent ~10-15% tail latency regression under mixed short+long batches.

Sam: Ugh. Same config as the canary or did you flip any kernel hints?

Erin: Canary + kernel hint toggle. Baseline used fused-attn + int8 matmul; experiment forced generic matmul path to test fragging behavior. Regression only shows up when paged KV fragmentation > ~28% and num_key_value_heads set to 4.

Jia: Interesting — do you have the flame or the pprof? Could be GQA vs MQA head steering the kernel selector into suboptimal kernels.

Erin: Pasted the short log and a flame snippet below (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17T08:12:01Z] sample: batch=32 mix(len=8..1024) mode=GQA heads=4 kv_dim=128 paged_frag=31% tail99=132ms -> 150ms
[2026-03-17T08:12:04Z] kernel: selected=generic_matmul fallback_of=fused_gemm cost_est=1.8
[2026-03-17T08:12:05Z] kv: page_loads/sec=42, avg_slots=512, fragmentation=0.31
```

Matt: That cost_est bump is telling. If the estimator uses per-head kv_dim heuristics it might over-score the generic path when heads*kv_dim crosses a threshold. Did you try increasing num_key_value_heads to 8? That moves the layout and sometimes flips the kernel selector back to fused paths.

Erin: I did a quick run at heads=8: tail99 back to ~120ms but throughput dropped ~6% for MQA workloads (longer sequences). So it's a tradeoff.

Sam: Could be cache locality — doubling heads changes the kv slot packing which reduces paged IO churn but increases per-step compute. We should try two short experiments: (1) keep heads=4 but increase kv_slot_size to reduce fragmentation; (2) keep kv_dim but hint kernel selector with a new kernel_hint flag.

Jia: Agreed. Also try a batching heuristic tweak: prefer grouping by kv_dim first for mixed batches so we don't force kernel churn mid-batch. Basically group short sequences together and long ones separately when mix_ratio > 0.25. That reduces cross-batch kernel switching.

Erin: Running variants now. Commands: 
```bash
./bench --model=mixtral-8x --mode=gqa --batcher=adaptive --group-by=kv_dim --kv_heads=4 --kv_slot_size=1024 --paged=true --kernel_hint=fused
```
Will drop results in perf-bot once finished.

perf-bot: Benchmark job 1937654321-variant-a finished. Summary: variant-a (kv_slot_size=1024, kernel_hint=fused) -> tail99: 126ms (-4% vs baseline), throughput +2% for GQA, MQA throughput unchanged.

Sam: Nice. Any sign of paged fragmentation moving?

perf-bot: Fragmentation dropped from 31% -> 18% on variant-a. Page loads/sec reduced by ~30%.

Matt: That aligns — larger slots reduce external fragmentation and paging. Kernel_hint seems to prevent the selector from choosing generic_matmul when fused is actually faster at our seq lengths.

Jia: For rollout I'd recommend: 1) default kv_slot_size bump to 1024 for mixtral-8x in paged mode, 2) expose kernel_hint as an opt-in route-level flag (so we can A/B), 3) add batching heuristic change to group by kv_dim when mixed short/long batches detected. We should also add an eval that simulates 20/80 short/long mix.

Erin: Agreed. I'll open a PR with the runtime patch (slot default + kernel_hint plumbing) and a perf test in the CI harness that reproduces the mixed-batch tail.

Sam: One more ask — can you capture a profiler with heads=4 but 'mock' kv_slot_size=1024 (no actual layout change) to isolate kernel selector vs true memory/layout effects?

Erin: Good call. Adding that to the test matrix.

Matt: If selector heuristics remain flaky, we should add a tiny runtime cost model tweak: penalize kernel switches within a batch by estimated switch overhead (microseconds) so grouping is preferred.

Jia: And record the rollout notes in release notes: why we changed default kv_slot_size and that kernel_hint exists for diagnostics.

Erin: I'll send the PR link here when ready and schedule a quick follow-up sync tomorrow after CI runs. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: CI perf tests queued: 1937654321-ci-1, 1937654321-ci-2.
